descriptions.value: A flaw was found in libssh. On servers with GSSAPIKeyExchange enabled, the gssapi-keyex path does not verify whether the authenticated Kerberos principal is authorized for the requested local user, allowing authenticated clients to log in as arbitrary users.

A flaw was found in ansible-core. The _extract_collection_from_git() function in ansible-core's concrete_artifact_manager.py constructs git clone commands without a '--' (end-of-options) separator before user-supplied URLs when installing collections from git sources. An attacker who provides a crafted collection source URI containing git argument injection payloads can achieve arbitrary command execution when a user runs 'ansible-galaxy collection install' with the malicious source. This is an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-11332, which hardened the role install path but missed the equivalent collection install code path.

Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity vulnerability in mtrudel bandit allows unauthenticated remote denial of service via CPU exhaustion during WebSocket fragment reassembly.

The size guard Bandit.WebSocket.Connection.oversize_message?/2 called from handle_frame/3 in lib/bandit/websocket/connection.ex appends each non-final continuation frame to a left-nested iolist and then re-measures the entire accumulated buffer with IO.iodata_length/1 on every frame. Because the buffer grows by one element per frame and is fully re-traversed each time, reassembly work is quadratic (O(n^2)) in the number of continuation frames.

The max_fragmented_message_size limit (default 8 MB) bounds total bytes but not frame count, and each frame can carry as little as one payload byte, so an attacker can send millions of tiny continuation frames using modest bandwidth to pin a CPU core for minutes to hours. Many concurrent connections can starve the whole server of CPU, denying service to legitimate users. The WebSocket read timeout does not help, because it is an idle timeout evaluated between reads and cannot preempt the synchronous reassembly work spent inside a single callback.

This issue affects bandit: from 1.11.0 before 1.12.1.

Vulnerabilidad de complejidad algorítmica ineficiente en mtrudel bandit permite la denegación de servicio remota no autenticada a través del agotamiento de la CPU durante el reensamblaje de fragmentos de WebSocket.

El guardia de tamaño ’Elixir.Bandit.WebSocket.Connection’:oversize_message?/2, llamado desde handle_frame/3 en lib/bandit/websocket/connection.ex, añade cada trama de continuación no final a una iolist anidada a la izquierda y luego vuelve a medir todo el búfer acumulado con IO.iodata_length/1 en cada trama. Debido a que el búfer crece en un elemento por trama y se vuelve a recorrer completamente cada vez, el trabajo de reensamblaje es cuadrático (O(n^2)) en el número de tramas de continuación.

El límite max_fragmented_message_size (predeterminado 8 MB) limita el total de bytes pero no el recuento de tramas, y cada trama puede transportar tan solo un byte de carga útil, por lo que un atacante puede enviar millones de pequeñas tramas de continuación utilizando un ancho de banda modesto para fijar un núcleo de CPU durante minutos u horas. Muchas conexiones concurrentes pueden privar de CPU a todo el servidor, denegando el servicio a usuarios legítimos. El tiempo de espera de lectura de WebSocket no ayuda, porque es un tiempo de espera inactivo evaluado entre lecturas y no puede anticipar el trabajo de reensamblaje síncrono realizado dentro de una única devolución de llamada.

Este problema afecta a bandit: desde 1.11.0 antes de 1.12.1.

Allocation of resources without limits vulnerability in ninenines cowlib allows an unauthenticated remote HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 peer to exhaust memory on the vulnerable server (or client) and cause a denial of service.

The HPACK and QPACK prefixed-integer decoder cow_hpack_common:dec_big_int/3 in src/cow_hpack_common.hrl (invoked from cow_hpack:decode/2 in src/cow_hpack.erl and from cow_qpack:decode_field_section/3 in src/cow_qpack.erl) reads continuation octets until it sees one whose high bit is clear, evaluating Int + (Value bsl M) at each step with the shift M growing by seven per octet. No limit is enforced on the number of continuation octets, on the resulting bit width, or on the value; the decoder consumes whatever encoded length the peer supplies.

Because Erlang integers are immutable, each intermediate Value bsl M and each accumulator update allocates a fresh bignum whose digit width grows linearly with the number of octets processed so far. Summed across the whole decode, the transient bignum digit materialization is on the order of the square of the encoded length. A single maximal HPACK indexed representation carried inside one HTTP/2 HEADERS plus one CONTINUATION frame at Cowboy's default max_frame_size_received can force hundreds of megabytes of transient allocation and garbage-collection churn before the resulting header-table index is rejected as invalid. Repeated or concurrent connections multiply the pressure and can drive the Erlang VM to memory exhaustion.

Cowlib is the HTTP parser used by Cowboy, RabbitMQ's management plugin, and other Erlang and Elixir HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 servers and clients, so any exposed endpoint that accepts HPACK or QPACK from an untrusted peer is reachable.

This issue affects cowlib: from 2.0.0-pre.1 before 2.19.0.

La vulnerabilidad de asignación de recursos sin límites en ninenines cowlib permite que un par HTTP/2 o HTTP/3 remoto no autenticado agote la memoria en el servidor (o cliente) vulnerable y cause una denegación de servicio.

El decodificador de enteros con prefijo HPACK y QPACK cow_hpack_common:dec_big_int/3 en src/cow_hpack_common.hrl (invocado desde cow_hpack:decode/2 en src/cow_hpack.erl y desde cow_qpack:decode_field_section/3 en src/cow_qpack.erl) lee octetos de continuación hasta que ve uno cuyo bit más significativo está claro, evaluando Int + (Value bsl M) en cada paso con el desplazamiento M creciendo en siete por octeto. No se impone ningún límite en el número de octetos de continuación, en el ancho de bits resultante o en el valor; el decodificador consume cualquier longitud codificada que el par suministre.

Debido a que los enteros de Erlang son inmutables, cada Value bsl M intermedio y cada actualización del acumulador asigna un nuevo bignum cuyo ancho de dígito crece linealmente con el número de octetos procesados hasta ahora. Sumado a lo largo de toda la decodificación, la materialización transitoria de dígitos bignum es del orden del cuadrado de la longitud codificada. Una única representación indexada HPACK máxima transportada dentro de un frame HTTP/2 HEADERS más un frame CONTINUATION en el max_frame_size_received predeterminado de Cowboy puede forzar cientos de megabytes de asignación transitoria y agitación de recolección de basura antes de que el índice de la tabla de encabezados resultante sea rechazado como inválido. Las conexiones repetidas o concurrentes multiplican la presión y pueden llevar a la VM de Erlang al agotamiento de la memoria.

Cowlib es el analizador HTTP utilizado por Cowboy, el plugin de gestión de RabbitMQ, y otros servidores y clientes HTTP/2 y HTTP/3 de Erlang y Elixir, por lo que cualquier punto final expuesto que acepte HPACK o QPACK de un par no confiable es alcanzable.

Este problema afecta a cowlib: desde 2.0.0 antes de 2.19.0.

Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in ninenines cowboy allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to exhaust connection process memory over HTTP/1.1.

The HTTP/1.1 handler in cowboy_http enforces the max_headers limit by counting the number of distinct header names in a map (maps:size(Headers)). When a request contains multiple header lines with the same name, the values are concatenated into a single ever-growing binary stored under that one map key (", " for regular headers, "; " for cookies), so the map size stays at one and the max_headers cap (default 100) is never reached. Because no accumulator bounds the total number of header lines or the total byte size of the header block (only per-line max_header_name_length and max_header_value_length apply), an unauthenticated client can send an arbitrary number of header lines with the same name and grow the connection process's binary memory to arbitrary size within the request window.

The impact per connection is bounded by request_timeout (default 5 seconds, not reset by header data), and by max_heap_size when set (the offending connection process is killed once its heap grows past the limit). When max_heap_size is left at the default (unset), sustained abuse can drive the Erlang VM into out-of-memory conditions.

This issue affects cowboy: from 2.0.0-pre.4 before 2.18.0.

Vulnerabilidad de asignación de recursos sin límites ni limitación en ninenines cowboy permite a un atacante remoto no autenticado agotar la memoria del proceso de conexión a través de HTTP/1.1.

El gestor HTTP/1.1 en cowboy_http aplica el límite max_headers contando el número de nombres de encabezado distintos en un mapa (maps:size(Headers)). Cuando una solicitud contiene múltiples líneas de encabezado con el mismo nombre, los valores se concatenan en un único binario en constante crecimiento almacenado bajo esa única clave de mapa (’, ’ para encabezados regulares, ’; ’ para cookies), por lo que el tamaño del mapa permanece en uno y el límite max_headers (predeterminado 100) nunca se alcanza. Debido a que ningún acumulador limita el número total de líneas de encabezado o el tamaño total en bytes del bloque de encabezado (solo se aplican max_header_name_length y max_header_value_length por línea), un cliente no autenticado puede enviar un número arbitrario de líneas de encabezado con el mismo nombre y aumentar la memoria binaria del proceso de conexión a un tamaño arbitrario dentro de la ventana de solicitud.

El impacto por conexión está limitado por request_timeout (predeterminado 5 segundos, no se restablece por los datos del encabezado), y por max_heap_size cuando se establece (el proceso de conexión infractor se termina una vez que su heap supera el límite). Cuando max_heap_size se deja en el valor predeterminado (no establecido), el abuso sostenido puede llevar a la VM de Erlang a condiciones de falta de memoria.

Este problema afecta a cowboy desde 2.0.0-pre.4 antes de 2.18.0.

Server-Side Request Forgery vulnerability in malach-it Boruta allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to cause the OAuth/OpenID authorization server to issue outbound HTTP requests to attacker-chosen URIs, including internal services and cloud metadata endpoints.

Three code paths fetch remote URIs supplied by the requester without sufficient validation of the target. Boruta.Oauth.Request.Base.fetch_unsigned_request/1 in lib/boruta/oauth/request/base.ex dereferences the OAuth request_uri parameter from the authorization request via Finch.build(:get, request_uri) |> Finch.request(OpenIDHttpClient). Boruta.Openid.parse_registration_params/2 in lib/boruta/openid.ex dereferences the jwks_uri supplied in an OpenID Connect dynamic client registration request. Boruta.Ecto.Clients.refresh_jwk_from_jwks_uri/1 in lib/boruta/adapters/ecto/clients.ex later refreshes the stored jwks_uri for an existing client. In all three paths the only validation is that the URI parses with a scheme (and one of the two request_uri clauses does not even restrict the scheme to http or https). The implementations do not require HTTPS, do not enforce a host or IP allowlist, do not reject loopback, private, link-local, or other non-public ranges after DNS resolution, do not cap response size, and do not constrain redirects. An attacker can therefore steer the server's HTTP client at arbitrary network targets reachable from the Boruta host.

This issue affects boruta: from 2.3.2 before 2.3.7 and from 3.0.0-beta.1 onward.

Una vulnerabilidad de falsificación de petición del lado del servidor en malach-it Boruta permite a un atacante remoto no autenticado causar que el servidor de autorización OAuth/OpenID emita peticiones HTTP salientes a URIs elegidas por el atacante, incluyendo servicios internos y puntos finales de metadatos en la nube.

Tres rutas de código obtienen URIs remotas suministradas por el solicitante sin validación suficiente del objetivo. Boruta.Oauth.Request.Base.fetch_unsigned_request/1 en lib/boruta/oauth/request/base.ex desreferencia el parámetro request_uri de OAuth de la petición de autorización a través de Finch.build(:get, request_uri) |> Finch.request(OpenIDHttpClient). Boruta.Openid.parse_registration_params/2 en lib/boruta/openid.ex desreferencia la jwks_uri suministrada en una petición de registro de cliente dinámico de OpenID Connect. Boruta.Ecto.Clients.refresh_jwk_from_jwks_uri/1 en lib/boruta/adapters/ecto/clients.ex posteriormente actualiza la jwks_uri almacenada para un cliente existente. En las tres rutas, la única validación es que la URI se analiza con un esquema (y una de las dos cláusulas de request_uri ni siquiera restringe el esquema a http o https). Las implementaciones no requieren HTTPS, no aplican una lista de permitidos de host o IP, no rechazan rangos de loopback, privados, link-local u otros rangos no públicos después de la resolución DNS, no limitan el tamaño de la respuesta y no restringen las redirecciones. Un atacante puede, por lo tanto, dirigir el cliente HTTP del servidor a objetivos de red arbitrarios alcanzables desde el host de Boruta.

Este problema afecta a boruta: desde 2.3.2 antes de 2.3.7.

Improper Isolation or Compartmentalization vulnerability in malach-it boruta (Boruta.Openid module) allows attackers to register OpenID Connect clients with administrative privileges through the dynamic client registration entry point. Boruta.Openid.register_client/3 forwards caller-supplied registration parameters to the administrative client creation path without a public/admin field-level allowlist, so an unauthenticated registrant can set security-sensitive attributes including supported grant types, authorized scopes, PKCE enforcement, public refresh and revocation behavior, token lifetimes, and signing settings. The library does not distinguish between metadata a public registrant is allowed to set and administrative controls that should require operator approval.

This vulnerability is associated with program files lib/boruta/openid.ex and program routines Boruta.Openid.register_client/3, Boruta.Openid.parse_registration_params/2.

This issue affects boruta: from 2.3.0 before 2.3.7 and from 3.0.0-beta.1 onward.

Vulnerabilidad de aislamiento o compartimentación inadecuados en malach-it boruta (módulo Elixir.Boruta.Openid) permite a los atacantes registrar clientes OpenID Connect con privilegios administrativos a través del punto de entrada de registro dinámico de clientes. Boruta.Openid.register_client/3 reenvía los parámetros de registro proporcionados por el llamante a la ruta de creación de clientes administrativos sin una lista de permitidos a nivel de campo público/administrador, por lo que un registrante no autenticado puede establecer atributos sensibles a la seguridad, incluyendo tipos de concesión soportados, alcances autorizados, aplicación de PKCE, comportamiento público de actualización y revocación, tiempos de vida de los tokens y configuraciones de firma. La biblioteca no distingue entre los metadatos que un registrante público puede establecer y los controles administrativos que deberían requerir la aprobación del operador.

Esta vulnerabilidad está asociada con los archivos de programa lib/boruta/openid.ex y las rutinas de programa ’Elixir.Boruta.Openid’:register_client/3, ’Elixir.Boruta.Openid’:parse_registration_params/2.

Este problema afecta a boruta desde 2.3.0 antes de 2.3.7.

A flaw was found in yggdrasil-worker-package-manager. A local attacker with existing access to the system could exploit an argument injection vulnerability in the APT backend. This allows specially crafted package names, which begin with a hyphen, to be misinterpreted as command options by apt-get. Successful exploitation could lead to remote code execution (RCE) with root privileges, enabling the attacker to fully compromise the system's integrity, confidentiality, and availability.

Se encontró una falla en yggdrasil-worker-package-manager. Un atacante local con acceso existente al sistema podría explotar una vulnerabilidad de inyección de argumentos en el backend de APT. Esto permite que nombres de paquetes especialmente diseñados, que comienzan con un guion, sean malinterpretados como opciones de comando por apt-get. La explotación exitosa podría conducir a ejecución remota de código (RCE) con privilegios de root, permitiendo al atacante comprometer completamente la integridad, confidencialidad y disponibilidad del sistema.

Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences vulnerability in ufirstgroup ymlr (Ymlr module) allows attackers to inject arbitrary content into generated YAML documents through document comments. Ymlr.document!/2 interpolates each caller-supplied comment string into the output behind a single # prefix without validating it or escaping line breaks. Because a YAML comment is terminated by a line break, the first carriage return or line feed in the comment string ends the comment context and everything after it is emitted at column 0 of the document body.

An attacker who controls text that the host application passes as a comment can forge top-level mapping keys, override values the application itself set, and emit --- or ... markers that split the output into additional documents. Downstream consumers of the generated YAML, such as configuration loaders, deployment manifests, CI pipelines and data importers, parse the injected content as legitimate data. The same clause backs Ymlr.document/2, Ymlr.documents!/2 and Ymlr.documents/2, so every document encoding entry point is affected.

This vulnerability is associated with program files lib/ymlr.ex and program routines Ymlr.document!/2, Ymlr.documents!/2.

This issue affects ymlr: from 0.0.1 before 5.1.6.

La vulnerabilidad de neutralización incorrecta de secuencias CRLF en ufirstgroup ymlr (módulo Elixir.Ymlr) permite a los atacantes inyectar contenido arbitrario en documentos YAML generados a través de comentarios de documentos. Ymlr.document!/2 interpola cada cadena de comentario proporcionada por el llamador en la salida detrás de un único prefijo # sin validarla o escapar los saltos de línea. Debido a que un comentario YAML termina con un salto de línea, el primer retorno de carro o salto de línea en la cadena de comentario finaliza el contexto del comentario y todo lo que le sigue se emite en la columna 0 del cuerpo del documento.

Un atacante que controla el texto que la aplicación anfitriona pasa como comentario puede falsificar claves de mapeo de nivel superior, anular valores que la propia aplicación estableció y emitir marcadores --- o ... que dividen la salida en documentos adicionales. Los consumidores posteriores del YAML generado, como cargadores de configuración, manifiestos de despliegue, pipelines de CI e importadores de datos, analizan el contenido inyectado como datos legítimos. La misma cláusula respalda Ymlr.document/2, Ymlr.documents!/2 y Ymlr.documents/2, por lo que cada punto de entrada de codificación de documentos se ve afectado.

Esta vulnerabilidad está asociada con los archivos de programa lib/ymlr.ex y las rutinas de programa Elixir.Ymlr:document!/2, Elixir.Ymlr:documents!/2.

Este problema afecta a ymlr desde 0.0.1 antes de 5.1.6.

Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling in ueberauth guardian allows denial of service via unbounded atom creation from attacker-influenced binary input.

Guardian.Plug.Keys derives connection and session namespace keys by passing arbitrary binaries to String.to_atom/1. base_key/1 in lib/guardian/plug/keys.ex converts any binary into the atom :"guardian_<input>", and the derived helpers claims_key/1, resource_key/1, and token_key/1 create a second atom on top of that. key_from_other/1 likewise converts a regex-captured binary through String.to_atom/1. The public specs advertise String.t() as a valid argument, so passing a string is documented usage, and higher-level entry points such as Guardian.Plug.current_token(conn, key: key) thread the caller-supplied key straight into these functions.

String.to_atom/1 creates a brand-new atom for every previously unseen binary, atoms are never garbage collected, and the BEAM atom table is fixed at roughly 1,048,576 entries by default. An application that routes attacker-influenced data (a tenant identifier, header, or other request input) into a Guardian key therefore mints one permanent atom per distinct value. A modest stream of varied, unauthenticated input permanently consumes the atom table and crashes the BEAM node, taking down every application running on it.

This issue affects guardian: from 0.1.0 before 2.4.1.

La asignación de recursos sin límites ni estrangulamiento en ueberauth guardian permite la denegación de servicio a través de la creación ilimitada de átomos a partir de entrada binaria influenciada por el atacante.

Guardian.Plug.Keys deriva claves de espacio de nombres de conexión y de sesión pasando binarios arbitrarios a String.to_atom/1. base_key/1 en lib/guardian/plug/keys.ex convierte cualquier binario en el átomo :“guardian_[input]”, y las funciones auxiliares derivadas claims_key/1, resource_key/1 y token_key/1 crean un segundo átomo además de eso. key_from_other/1 de manera similar convierte un binario capturado por regex a través de String.to_atom/1. Las especificaciones públicas anuncian String.t() como un argumento válido, por lo que pasar una cadena es un uso documentado, y los puntos de entrada de nivel superior, como Guardian.Plug.current_token(conn, key: key), pasan la clave proporcionada por el llamador directamente a estas funciones.

String.to_atom/1 crea un átomo completamente nuevo para cada binario no visto anteriormente, los átomos nunca son recolectados por el recolector de basura, y la tabla de átomos de BEAM está fijada en aproximadamente 1.048.576 entradas por defecto. Una aplicación que enruta datos influenciados por el atacante (un identificador de inquilino, encabezado u otra entrada de solicitud) en una clave de Guardian, por lo tanto, acuña un átomo permanente por cada valor distinto. Un flujo modesto de entrada variada y no autenticada consume permanentemente la tabla de átomos y bloquea el nodo BEAM, derribando todas las aplicaciones que se ejecutan en él.

Este problema afecta a guardian: desde 0.1.0 antes de 2.4.1.

Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling in ueberauth guardian allows denial of service via unbounded atom creation from attacker-controlled binary input.

Guardian.Permissions.AtomEncoding encodes permission scopes by passing arbitrary binaries to String.to_atom/1. When encode/3 in lib/guardian/permissions/atom_encoding.ex is called with a list, each binary entry is handled by the encode_value/3 binary clause, which calls String.to_atom(value) with no allow-list check. The perm_set argument (the application's small, finite set of legitimate permission names) is discarded, so any external string flows straight into atom creation. This encoder is selected with use Guardian.Permissions, encoding: Guardian.Permissions.AtomEncoding and reached through the imported encode/3 entry point.

String.to_atom/1 creates a brand-new atom for every previously unseen binary, atoms are never garbage collected, and the BEAM atom table is fixed at roughly 1,048,576 entries by default. An application that funnels attacker-influenced permission scopes (from a request body, a JWT claim, or other external input) into encode/3 therefore mints one permanent atom per distinct value. A modest stream of varied, unauthenticated input permanently consumes the atom table and crashes the BEAM node with system_limit, taking down every application running on it.

The default encoder is Guardian.Permissions.BitwiseEncoding, which is not affected.

This issue affects guardian: from 2.0.0 before 2.4.1.

La asignación de recursos sin límites ni estrangulamiento en ueberauth guardian permite la denegación de servicio a través de la creación ilimitada de átomos a partir de entrada binaria controlada por el atacante.

Guardian.Permissions.AtomEncoding codifica los ámbitos de permiso pasando binarios arbitrarios a String.to_atom/1. Cuando se llama a encode/3 en lib/guardian/permissions/atom_encoding.ex con una lista, cada entrada binaria es manejada por la cláusula binaria encode_value/3, que llama a String.to_atom(value) sin una verificación de lista de permitidos. El argumento perm_set (el conjunto pequeño y finito de nombres de permiso legítimos de la aplicación) se descarta, por lo que cualquier cadena externa fluye directamente a la creación de átomos. Este codificador se selecciona con use Guardian.Permissions, encoding: Guardian.Permissions.AtomEncoding y se alcanza a través del punto de entrada importado encode/3.

String.to_atom/1 crea un átomo completamente nuevo para cada binario no visto previamente, los átomos nunca son recolectados por el recolector de basura, y la tabla de átomos de BEAM está fijada en aproximadamente 1.048.576 entradas por defecto. Una aplicación que canaliza ámbitos de permiso influenciados por el atacante (desde un cuerpo de solicitud, una declaración JWT u otra entrada externa) en encode/3, por lo tanto, acuña un átomo permanente por cada valor distinto. Un flujo modesto de entrada variada y no autenticada consume permanentemente la tabla de átomos y bloquea el nodo BEAM con system_limit, derribando todas las aplicaciones que se ejecutan en él.

El codificador predeterminado es Guardian.Permissions.BitwiseEncoding, el cual no se ve afectado.

Este problema afecta a guardian: desde la versión 2.0.0 hasta antes de la 2.4.1.

Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in ueberauth guardian (Guardian.Permissions module) allows a denial of service via BEAM atom-table exhaustion.

This vulnerability is associated with program file lib/guardian/permissions.ex and program routines Guardian.Permissions.encode_permissions!/1, Guardian.Permissions.encode_permissions_into_claims!/2, Guardian.Permissions.do_encode_permissions!/2.

The Guardian.Permissions mixin installs a public encode_permissions!/1 function on every module that does use Guardian.Permissions. For each key of the supplied map, encode_permissions!/1 calls String.to_atom(to_string(k)) before any validation runs. The integer-value clause of do_encode_permissions!/2 then short-circuits straight to encoding without validating the key against the configured permission set, so a key with an integer value is interned as a fresh atom with no exception raised. Atoms are never garbage collected and the BEAM atom table is a fixed-size resource (default roughly 1,048,576 entries), so each unique attacker-chosen key permanently consumes one slot. An attacker who can influence a permission map that reaches encode_permissions!/1 (for example a permissions map read from a request body and passed into token issuance via encode_permissions_into_claims!/2) can mint an unbounded number of atoms and exhaust the atom table, crashing the entire BEAM node and every service running on it. The sibling decode_permissions/1 is not affected because it skips keys absent from the configured permission set.

This issue affects guardian: from 1.0.0-beta.0 before 2.4.1.

La vulnerabilidad de asignación de recursos sin límites ni limitación en ueberauth guardian (módulo Guardian.Permissions) permite una denegación de servicio a través del agotamiento de la tabla de átomos de BEAM.

Esta vulnerabilidad está asociada con el archivo de programa lib/guardian/permissions.ex y las rutinas de programa ’Elixir.Guardian.Permissions’:encode_permissions!/1, ’Elixir.Guardian.Permissions’:encode_permissions_into_claims!/2, ’Elixir.Guardian.Permissions’:do_encode_permissions!/2.

El mixin Guardian.Permissions instala una función pública encode_permissions!/1 en cada módulo que utiliza Guardian.Permissions. Para cada clave del mapa proporcionado, encode_permissions!/1 llama a String.to_atom(to_string(k)) antes de que se ejecute cualquier validación. La cláusula de valor entero de do_encode_permissions!/2 entonces hace un cortocircuito directamente a la codificación sin validar la clave contra el conjunto de permisos configurado, por lo que una clave con un valor entero se interna como un átomo nuevo sin que se genere ninguna excepción. Los átomos nunca son recolectados por el recolector de basura y la tabla de átomos de BEAM es un recurso de tamaño fijo (por defecto, aproximadamente 1.048.576 entradas), por lo que cada clave única elegida por el atacante consume permanentemente una ranura. Un atacante que puede influir en un mapa de permisos que llega a encode_permissions!/1 (por ejemplo, un mapa de permisos leído de un cuerpo de solicitud y pasado a la emisión de tokens a través de encode_permissions_into_claims!/2) puede acuñar un número ilimitado de átomos y agotar la tabla de átomos, colapsando todo el nodo BEAM y cada servicio que se ejecuta en él. El hermano decode_permissions/1 no se ve afectado porque omite las claves ausentes del conjunto de permisos configurado.

Este problema afecta a guardian: desde 2.0.0 antes de 2.4.1.

Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature in ueberauth guardian allows an unauthenticated attacker to revoke a victim's session with a forged token.

Guardian.revoke/3 in lib/guardian.ex decodes the supplied token with peek/1, which performs no signature verification (it only base64-decodes the JWT header and payload). The resulting unverified claims are forwarded directly to the configured token module's revoke callback and the implementation's on_revoke callback, a state-mutating sink. The sibling operations refresh/2 and exchange/4 both call decode_and_verify first, so the signature is checked before anything acts on the claims; revoke/3 is the only state-mutating path that acts on claims without verifying the signature.

An attacker who knows or guesses a victim's identifying claim values (jti, sub) can forge a JWT carrying those claims, sign it with an arbitrary key, and submit it to any endpoint that funnels a caller-supplied token into Guardian.revoke/3 (the standard logout / session-revocation pattern). When the token module mutates state keyed by the claims (whitelist deletion or blacklist insertion, for example a GuardianDb-style store), the victim's legitimate session is evicted. This is an unauthenticated session-revocation denial of service; the attacker never needs the signing secret.

This issue affects guardian: from 1.0.0-beta.0 before 2.4.1.

Verificación Incorrecta de Firma Criptográfica en ueberauth guardian permite a un atacante no autenticado revocar la sesión de una víctima con un token falsificado.

Guardian.revoke/3 en lib/guardian.ex decodifica el token suministrado con peek/1, que no realiza verificación de firma (solo decodifica en base64 el encabezado y la carga útil del JWT). Las reclamaciones no verificadas resultantes se reenvían directamente a la devolución de llamada ’revoke’ del módulo de token configurado y a la devolución de llamada ’on_revoke’ de la implementación, un sumidero que muta el estado. Las operaciones hermanas refresh/2 y exchange/4 ambas llaman primero a decode_and_verify, por lo que la firma se verifica antes de que cualquier cosa actúe sobre las reclamaciones; revoke/3 es la única ruta que muta el estado y que actúa sobre las reclamaciones sin verificar la firma.

Un atacante que conoce o adivina los valores de reclamación identificativos de una víctima (jti, sub) puede falsificar un JWT que contenga esas reclamaciones, firmarlo con una clave arbitraria y enviarlo a cualquier punto final que canalice un token suministrado por el llamador a Guardian.revoke/3 (el patrón estándar de cierre de sesión / revocación de sesión). Cuando el módulo de token muta el estado indexado por las reclamaciones (eliminación de lista blanca o inserción en lista negra, por ejemplo, un almacén estilo GuardianDb), la sesión legítima de la víctima es expulsada. Esto es una denegación de servicio de revocación de sesión no autenticada; el atacante nunca necesita el secreto de firma.

Este problema afecta a guardian: desde 1.0.0 antes de 2.4.1.

A flaw was found in udisks2. A local attacker with an active console session can exploit insufficient authorization checking on the 'as-user' option in the org.freedesktop.UDisks2.Filesystem.Mount() D-Bus method. This allows the attacker to spoof the 'as-user' parameter, mounting filesystems on behalf of arbitrary users, including privileged accounts. This can lead to local privilege escalation through mount point injection and manipulation of the mount namespace visible to privileged users.

descriptions.value: A heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability exists in the GIMP DDS (DirectDraw Surface) file parser. When a crafted DDS file declares a D3D9 pixel format but sets a lower bits-per-pixel (bpp) value in the header, the loader allocates an undersized heap buffer. Subsequent pixel data consumption at the real format's stride causes a write past the heap buffer boundary, leading to heap metadata corruption and potential code execution.

Multiple integer overflow and underflow vulnerabilities were found in the GStreamer gst-plugins-ugly ASF demuxer (asfdemux) when parsing header objects from crafted ASF, WMV, or WMA files. Insufficient validation of attacker-controlled length and size values can bypass bounds checks and cause out-of-bounds heap reads. This can result in application crash, denial of service, or limited information disclosure when untrusted media is processed.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in the GIMP image manipulation program, specifically within its Seattle Filmworks file loader. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by tricking a user into opening a specially crafted Seattle Filmworks file. This could lead to a heap overflow, allowing the attacker to write several kilobytes of controlled data beyond the intended memory buffer. Such an overflow can result in memory corruption, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution or a denial of service.

A flaw was found in GIMP's PSD file format plugin. This vulnerability, an unsigned integer underflow in the `block_rem` variable, occurs when a user opens a specially crafted `.psd` image file. The underflow leads to parser confusion, enabling an attacker to inject arbitrary data as layer resource blocks. This can ultimately result in arbitrary code execution, allowing the attacker to run malicious code on the victim's system.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in GIMP's file format plugins, including those for PSD and PAA files. A remote attacker could exploit these vulnerabilities by tricking a user into opening a specially crafted image file. A flaw was found in libvirt. A local attacker, specifically a process running as the confined `swtpm` user, could exploit a symlink-following vulnerability in the `virFileChownFiles()` function. By planting a symbolic link within the `swtpm` state directory, the attacker could trick the root-level libvirt daemon into changing the ownership of an arbitrary file to the `swtpm` user. This allows for privilege escalation from the `swtpm` sandbox to root-level file ownership control.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in the ChunkReader component of the Undertow HTTP server, which is used by WildFly and JBoss EAP to handle chunked transfer encoding. The issue occurs because the parser uses a single internal variable to store both the remaining chunk size and state flags. By sending a specially crafted request with an extremely large chunk size, an attacker can cause these values to overlap, tricking the parser into thinking a request has finished prematurely. This can allow a second, "smuggled" request to be processed out of sync, potentially bypassing security controls.

descriptions.value:
A flaw was found in DBI. This is a fix for a partial fix for CVE-2026-14380 for RHEL 9.8.z and 10.2.z.

For a detailed Statement, Description and Mitigation please reffer to the original https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/cve-2026-19546.

A flaw was found in libvirt. An unprivileged local user could exploit an integer overflow vulnerability in the NodeGetFreePages RPC handler. This flaw allows crafted values to bypass a size check, leading to an undersized memory buffer. Subsequently, real NUMA node data can overwrite this buffer. This heap buffer overflow can corrupt the root libvirt daemon's memory, potentially leading to a denial of service or local privilege escalation.

Se encontró un fallo en libvirt. Un usuario local sin privilegios podría explotar una vulnerabilidad de desbordamiento de entero en el gestor RPC NodeGetFreePages. Este fallo permite que valores manipulados eludan una comprobación de tamaño, lo que lleva a un búfer de memoria de tamaño insuficiente. Posteriormente, los datos reales del nodo NUMA pueden sobrescribir este búfer. Este desbordamiento de búfer en el heap puede corromper la memoria del demonio root de libvirt, lo que podría llevar a una denegación de servicio o una escalada de privilegios local.

descriptions.value: A privilege escalation flaw was found in FreeIPA. The uniqueness constraint enforced on Kerberos principal name attributes in the 389-ds directory server does not properly account for equivalent representations of the same principal name, allowing a user with sufficient LDAP write privileges to create a service principal that impersonates an existing privileged one. This can lead to unauthorized acquisition of Kerberos service tickets for sensitive services, potentially resulting in full domain compromise.

Se encontró una vulnerabilidad de escalada de privilegios en FreeIPA. La restricción de unicidad aplicada a los atributos de nombre de principal de Kerberos en el servidor de directorio 389-ds no tiene en cuenta adecuadamente las representaciones equivalentes del mismo nombre de principal, permitiendo a un usuario con suficientes privilegios de escritura LDAP crear un principal de servicio que suplanta a uno privilegiado existente. Esto puede llevar a la adquisición no autorizada de tickets de servicio de Kerberos para servicios sensibles, lo que podría resultar en un compromiso total del dominio.

descriptions.value: A vulnerability was found in RPM's rpmbuild tarball processing. When processing a crafted source archive, the getTarSpec() function in tools/rpmbuild.cc passes an attacker-controlled tar archive member name to rpmExpand() as part of a %{basename:...} macro expression. A specially crafted .spec member name can therefore inject RPM macros, including Lua expressions, resulting in arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the user running rpmbuild. This can be exploited when a victim or automated build system processes an attacker-controlled source tarball using rpmbuild tarball mode (such as -ts, -ta, or -tb).

Se encontró una vulnerabilidad en el procesamiento de tarballs de rpmbuild de RPM. Al procesar un archivo fuente manipulado, la función getTarSpec() en tools/rpmbuild.cc pasa un nombre de miembro de archivo tar controlado por el atacante a rpmExpy() como parte de una expresión de macro %{basename:...}. Un nombre de miembro .spec especialmente manipulado puede, por lo tanto, inyectar macros de RPM, incluyendo expresiones Lua, resultando en ejecución de código arbitrario con los privilegios del usuario que ejecuta rpmbuild. Esto puede ser explotado cuando una víctima o un sistema de compilación automatizado procesa un tarball fuente controlado por el atacante usando el modo tarball de rpmbuild (como -ts, -ta o -tb).

descriptions.value: NetworkManager did not apply the private_user restriction to the 802-1x.ca-path and phase2-ca-path directory-valued connection properties. This incomplete fix for CVE-2025-9615 allows an unprivileged local user to point a private WPA-Enterprise (802.1X) connection profile's CA path at an attacker-controlled directory, bypassing server certificate validation and enabling credential theft via a rogue access point.

NetworkManager no aplicó la restricción private_user a las propiedades de conexión con valores de directorio 802-1x.ca-path y phase2-ca-path. Esta solución incompleta para CVE-2025-9615 permite a un usuario local sin privilegios apuntar la ruta de CA de un perfil de conexión WPA-Enterprise (802.1X) privado a un directorio controlado por el atacante, eludiendo la validación del certificado del servidor y permitiendo el robo de credenciales a través de un punto de acceso malicioso.

A flaw was found in the file-pcx plugin in GIMP, affecting 32-bit builds only. When processing a PCX image file, the plugin calculates memory allocation sizes based on the image dimensions and the number of color planes. If a crafted file sets the number of planes to 4 alongside sufficiently large dimensions, the calculation exceeds the 32-bit integer limit and overflows, resulting in an undersized heap-based buffer allocation. This integer overflow issue results in a heap-based buffer overflow when the plugin subsequently writes image data into the undersized buffer, causing memory corruption, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution or a denial of service.

Se encontró una falla en el plugin file-pcx en GIMP, que afecta solo a las compilaciones de 32 bits. Al procesar un archivo de imagen PCX, el plugin calcula los tamaños de asignación de memoria basándose en las dimensiones de la imagen y el número de planos de color. Si un archivo manipulado establece el número de planos en 4 junto con dimensiones suficientemente gryes, el cálculo excede el límite de entero de 32 bits y se desborda, lo que resulta en una asignación de búfer basada en montículo de tamaño insuficiente. Este problema de desbordamiento de entero resulta en un desbordamiento de búfer basado en montículo cuando el plugin escribe posteriormente datos de imagen en el búfer de tamaño insuficiente, causando corrupción de memoria, lo que podría conducir a la ejecución de código arbitrario o a una denegación de servicio.

A stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability exists in BlueZ, the Linux Bluetooth protocol stack. A remote user within Bluetooth radio range can send a specially crafted Extended Inquiry Response (EIR) packet that causes a buffer overflow when the target device performs Bluetooth discovery. This vulnerability can lead to a Denial of Service (DoS) by crashing the bluetoothd service and may allow for arbitrary code execution.

A flaw was found in Undertow. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending specially crafted WebSocket messages with permessage-deflate negotiated. This could lead to excessive memory consumption due to the PerMessageDeflateFunction.largerBuffer() method using exponential doubling, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) for the affected application.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in Jolokia's JSR-160 proxy functionality where insufficient validation of client-controlled JMX service URLs allows a bypass of the denylist introduced to mitigate CVE-2018-1000130. The proxy accepts a `target.url` value from a Jolokia POST request and passes it to `JMXServiceURL` and `JMXConnectorFactory` for establishing the remote JMX connection. The existing denylist only rejects URLs matching `service:jmx:rmi:///jndi/ldap:.*`, which can be bypassed using alternative valid JMX service URL forms, including `ldaps://` schemes or LDAP URLs with a non-empty JMX host component. These URLs are accepted as valid `JMXServiceURL` objects and can cause the Jolokia agent JVM to perform a JNDI lookup against an attacker-controlled LDAP endpoint. This can result in server-side request forgery (SSRF), forwarding of supplied JMX credentials to the remote endpoint, and potentially remote code execution depending on the classes and configuration available in the target JVM.

descriptions.value: The nsenter --join-cgroup option opens the target cgroup.procs file as root and leaves that file descriptor open across later namespace and credential changes and across execve(). Because the kernel checks later cgroup migrations using the credentials from the original open, a program run in an attacker-controlled target can inherit root's ability to move host processes between cgroups. After a privileged operator uses --join-cgroup against that target, an unprivileged user can migrate and terminate unrelated root processes.

The X-mount.subdir option uses a detached-tree fast path on Linux 6.15 and later and passes the configured subdirectory to open_tree() with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW. That flag does not stop intermediate symlink traversal or keep resolution inside the newly mounted filesystem. A local unprivileged user with an fstab-authorized X-mount.subdir entry can attach a host path at the intended mountpoint.

A flaw was found in util-linux. Restricted bind mounts take the source path from fstab but do not pin that source before the privileged mount. A local unprivileged user who can replace the authorized source or a writable ancestor can redirect SUID mount(8) to bind another host directory. If the fstab entry also sets X-mount.owner, X-mount.group, or X-mount.mode, root then changes ownership or mode on that redirected inode.

A flaw was found in libsoup. A malicious HTTP/2 server or a Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attacker can exploit a heap use-after-free vulnerability in the HTTP/2 client implementation. This occurs when a GNOME application uploads a file using HTTP/2, and the server sends a GOAWAY frame while the file body is being read asynchronously. This can lead to memory corruption, potentially resulting in information disclosure or arbitrary code execution.

A privilege escalation flaw was found in the scan_mysql actor of leapp-upgrade-el9toel10 (provided by leapp-repository). During RHEL 9 to RHEL 10 upgrades, the actor runs:
mysqld --validate-config --log-error-verbosity=2 directly as root in the Leapp actor context, bypassing the packaged MySQL systemd unit that normally starts the daemon as User=mysql.

A process compromised as the mysql OS identity can write a version-2 persisted configuration (mysqld-auto.cnf) and a malicious shared object into /var/lib/mysql (a directory owned by mysql). That persisted map can set plugin_dir to /var/lib/mysql and early_plugin_load (or related loader options such as plugin_load / plugin_load_add) so MySQL loads the attacker-controlled object during configuration validation. Plugin loading can reach dlopen() before MySQL’s runtime-user check and before plugin-symbol validation.

When an administrator subsequently runs the documented Leapp preupgrade or upgrade workflow, attacker-controlled code can execute as UID 0 with a full capability set in an unconfined SELinux domain (unconfined_t). The attack does not require write access to the default system plugin path under /usr; redirecting plugin_dir via mysql-owned persisted state is sufficient. Ordinary SQL privileges alone (including highly privileged SQL accounts) are not a sufficient startpoint — OS-level execution as the mysql service identity is required, plus later administrator invocation of Leapp.

A vulnerability in CRI-O checkpoint restore allows a user who can create a pod from a malicious checkpointed container to bypass the destination Kubernetes security context. The restored process may retain credentials, Linux capabilities, no_new_privs, and seccomp state from the checkpoint instead of enforcing the destination configuration. This can allow execution with elevated privileges across the container security boundary.
Affected upstream supported versions are CRI-O 1.34 and later. Downstream Red Hat products are affected from OCP 4.17 onward. Fixes have been applied to supported branches but are not yet released.
Exploitation requires permission to create a pod from a malicious checkpoint image and checkpoint restore functionality to be available.

A flaw was found in pki-core. The v2 REST ACL filter selects a tie-breaking permission for colliding literal and wildcard ACL keys using lexicographic string comparison rather than specificity, causing a wildcard-mapped permission to override a more specific literal-mapped permission when both match. In the CA's profile-management REST API this allows a request to POST /v2/profiles/raw -- intended to require Administrator-level profiles.create permission -- to instead be authorized under the lower-privileged profiles.approve permission held by the default Certificate Manager Agents group. The highest threat from this vulnerability is to confidentiality and integrity of the certificate authority's issuance policy.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in 389-ds-base. An unauthenticated remote attacker can send a complete LDAP operation followed by the first bytes of an incomplete LDAPMessage on the same connection, causing the server to hand that connection to a second worker thread before the first worker's result is flushed. The second worker blocks until nsslapd-ioblocktimeout while holding the connection mutex, preventing delivery of the completed operation's result. Repeating this across a small number of connections proportional to the configured worker-thread pool size exhausts the entire pool under default configuration, denying service to all clients (anonymous and authenticated, plaintext and TLS) for as long as the attacker maintains the connections.

A flaw was found in Dogtag PKI (pki-core). The CMCAuthForEST authentication plugin fails open when an EST fullcmc enrollment request is submitted via BasicAuth without an end-user TLS client certificate. The SSL_CLIENT_CERT session attribute retains the EST subsystem's agent certificate, which causes downstream authorization checks to treat the request as agent-privileged. An authenticated EST user can exploit this to obtain CA-signed certificates with arbitrary subject names.

A flaw was found in sssd. A remote attacker can cause a denial of service (DoS) by submitting a certificate that lacks an expected Security Identifier (SID) extension. In deployments configured with SID-based certificate mapping rules, the service fails to verify the presence of the extension before processing it, causing the process to crash during authentication or lookup operations.

A flaw was found in SSSD. When configured to evaluate password expiration warnings before restrictive access rules in LDAP (Lightweight Directory Access Protocol) environments, an expired-password warning terminates rule evaluation early and treats the access request as successful. A remote authenticated user with an expired password using an alternative authentication method, such as SSH public key authentication, can exploit this flaw to bypass access control restrictions and gain unauthorized access to protected systems.

A flaw was found in SSSD. An unprivileged local user can repeatedly request lookups for nonexistent entries through the Name Service Switch (NSS) responder. Because the negative cache does not limit the total number of stored entries and only removes expired records when an existing key is rechecked, the cache can grow without bound. This behavior can lead to memory exhaustion, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) as the responder becomes unresponsive or terminates.

A flaw was found in sssd. A local attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending a crafted Pluggable Authentication Module (PAM) request containing a zero-length authentication token to the responder socket. Due to missing input validation, the service attempts to read beyond buffer boundaries when processing the token, causing the PAM responder to crash.

A flaw was found in SSSD. A local attacker with access to the Name Service Switch (NSS) responder UNIX socket can trigger an integer underflow by sending a specially crafted request with an undersized packet header. This issue causes an out-of-bounds memory read during packet parsing, crashing the responder process and resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

A heap-based buffer overflow was found in GIMP’s DirectDraw Surface (DDS) loader. When loading a crafted DDS image, buffer sizes derived from width, height, and pitch can be computed using 32-bit arithmetic that overflows. The allocated buffer is too small for the amount of pixel data written through GEGL, following integer overflow in size calculations. This may allow heap corruption and, in the worst case, arbitrary code execution in the context of the GIMP process.

A flaw was found in ansible-core. When installing a collection with `ansible-galaxy collection install`, the archive extractor validates member paths using lexical path normalisation (os.path.abspath) instead of resolving symbolic links (os.path.realpath), and it performs no containment check on symlink-typed directory members before creating them. A crafted collection tarball can chain symlink directory entries so that a subsequent file member is written outside the intended destination directory. This allows an attacker who can get a victim to install a malicious collection to overwrite arbitrary files with the privileges of the user running ansible-galaxy, leading to code execution on the control node. This is a bypass of the fix for CVE-2020-10691.

A flaw was found in GNU patch. An attacker can achieve arbitrary file creation outside the intended working directory by enticing a user or automated workflow to apply a specially crafted patch file. Due to missing validation during automatic patch reversal, absolute file paths in patch headers are accepted rather than rejected. Consequently, the utility can create files in arbitrary locations with the permissions of the executing user.

descriptions.value: An access control bypass flaw was identified in Samba's vfs_ceph_rgw module in it's openat() function. An authenticated user can bypass access controls to read or overwrite restricted files on shares configured with the experimental vfs_ceph_rgw module. When a client requests an existing file using mismatched character casing, the module fails to perform a case-insensitive lookup correctly, causing the server to treat the operation as creating a new file. As a result, the server skips standard permission checks on the existing file, allowing the attacker to access or overwrite sensitive data owned by other users.

A flaw was found in dnsmasq. When following a CNAME in a DNS response, the resolver can cache records for the CNAME target without checking that those records belong to the responding server's authorized zone. In split-DNS deployments that send some domains to a specific upstream, an attacker who controls that upstream can inject cache entries for unrelated names. Later clients may then receive attacker-chosen addresses for those names.

A flaw was found in glib-networking. When establishing connections using Transport Layer Security (TLS) version 1.3, the client-side session cache does not limit the number of session tickets retained for a single host. A malicious server can exploit this by sending excessive session ticket messages, causing the client application to continuously consume memory. This unbounded memory growth can exhaust system memory, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

A flaw was found in json-glib. The JSONPath slice evaluator used by json_path_query() can enter an infinite loop when given a slice expression with a negative step. An application that evaluates attacker-controlled JSONPath expressions can be forced into a hang, leading to a denial of service.

A flaw was found in libslirp in icmp_forward_error(). When building an ICMP error response, the length of the quoted original IPv4 packet was taken from the IP header without clamping it to the actual buffer length. A truncated or malformed packet could cause an out-of-bounds heap read, leaking host memory into the ICMP error packet returned to a guest or container.

descriptions.value: OpenEMR before 8.4.0 contains a mass assignment vulnerability in the patient portal OnsiteDocument query API that lets request parameters set bitwise criteria filters whose values are placed unquoted into the SQL WHERE clause. Authenticated patient portal users can inject SQL via parameters such as Id_BitwiseAnd to read any database table, including other patients' records and staff password hashes.

OpenEMR from 7.0.1 before 8.4.0 contains a flaw in src/Common/Auth/OneTimeAuth.php that ignores the enforce_onetime_use and max_access_count flags, never revokes consumed service_auth tokens, and checks login_pin without rate limiting or strict comparison. Attackers holding a captured token can replay it or brute-force the PIN to open patient-portal sessions exposing PHI.

OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the FaxSMS module's RCFaxClient and SignalWireClient disposeDocument functions that allows authenticated low-privilege users to read and overwrite arbitrary files via the unsanitized file_path parameter. Attackers can request action=download to retrieve cleartext files like sqlconf.php database credentials and keys, or use action=setup to overwrite web-server-writable files with ciphertext.

OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in OnsitePortalActivityController::Update() that checks the request's patientId instead of the stored record's owner. Authenticated portal patients can send PUT requests to the onsiteportalactivity API with another patient's activity id and their own patientId to disclose tableArgs and checksum data, overwrite narratives and status, and take ownership of the record.

OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the CCDA/CCD preview stylesheets, where cda.xsl copies event-handler attributes whose values evade a character denylist and ccd.xsl copies table-cell attributes unsanitized into preview HTML. Authenticated users can upload a crafted CCDA/CCD document with onmouseover, onclick, or onfocus handlers to execute script in a clinician's session when previewed.

OpenEMR before 8.4.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in FHIR Media/:uuid and QuestionnaireResponse read routes that skip ACL checks. Non-patient API tokens lacking OpenEMR ACLs can request resources by uuid, bypassing compartment filtering to read any patient's documents and questionnaire responses.

OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains a broken access control and path traversal vulnerability in the fax/sms module disposeDocument action via an unvalidated file_path parameter. Authenticated low-privilege users can read sqlconf.php to recover database credentials and write arbitrary files as the web user, enabling remote code execution.

OpenEMR before 8.4.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in its SMART on FHIR implementation because checkUserHasAccessToPatient() in BearerTokenAuthorizationStrategy.php unconditionally returns true. Authenticated users or malicious SMART apps can manipulate token launch context to bind requests to arbitrary patient UUIDs, gaining unauthorized read/write access to other patients' FHIR resources.

OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in interface/forms/eye_mag/report.php that allows authenticated users to inject scripts by adding unescaped document notes. Attackers with document-note write access can store malicious JavaScript in a retina document note that executes when clinicians generate the Eye Exam patient report, exposing session cookies.

OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in portal/lib/persist.php that allows authenticated portal patients to write settings for other patients. Attackers can modify the setting_patient parameter in a JSON POST request to another patient's PID, altering that patient's portal settings such as the portal theme.

OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in OnsiteDocumentController::Query() that allows authenticated portal patients to read other patients' documents by overriding Pid_Equals criteria. Attackers can supply Pid_Equals, Pid_GreaterThan, or Pid_In request parameters to the onsitedocuments API to retrieve signed consent forms, signatures, and PHI of any patient.

OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains missing authorization and insecure direct object reference vulnerabilities in the oe-module-prior-authorizations module that allow authenticated low-privilege users to access and modify other patients' records. Attackers can request public/reports/list_report.php to view all patients' names, MRNs, insurance and prior-auth data, or submit arbitrary id values to public/index.php to overwrite other patients' prior-authorization records.

OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in interface/billing/sl_eob_process.php that allows authenticated users to write and read files by supplying unsanitized eraname values. Attackers without billing privileges can inject ../ sequences to create ERA report .html files anywhere the web user can write and parse arbitrary .edi files echoed into the report.

OpenEMR before 8.4.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the FHIR GET /fhir/Person/:uuid route that allows patient-portal users to read any staff member's demographics by bypassing compartment enforcement. Attackers holding a patient SMART token with patient/Person.read can harvest staff Person UUIDs from Appointment references to retrieve names, home addresses, phone numbers, and personal emails.

OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in many encounter-form view and save endpoints that lack patient/encounter ownership checks. Authenticated clinical users can enumerate sequential form id values in requests such as soap/view.php and save.php to read and overwrite other patients' clinical records.

OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in PortalPatientController::Read() that allows authenticated patients to read other patients' pending demographic change requests. Attackers can supply another patient's ID in the patientId query string parameter to retrieve PHI including names, addresses, SSNs, and insurance information.

OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in library/ajax/upload.php that allows any authenticated user to read and overwrite document data by supplying an arbitrary doc_id. Low-privilege users can enumerate doc_id values with the fetch and save actions to disclose patient health information and tamper with medical records across all patients.

OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in OnsiteDocumentController::Query() that allows authenticated portal patients to bypass the lowercase pid authorization guard by supplying a capitalised Pid parameter. Attackers can request the api/onsitedocuments endpoint with Pid set to another patient's id to overwrite the session-pinned criteria and read other patients' onsite documents containing PHI.

A flaw was found in GStreamer's adaptive streaming demuxers (HLS, DASH, MSS). When processing a media playlist or manifest, URIs referenced in the manifest content are fetched without restricting which URI schemes are permitted. An attacker who controls a manifest URL, or who can inject content into an HTTP manifest response, can include file:// URIs pointing to arbitrary local files, causing the affected application to read and process those files. In automated or server-side deployments such as media recorders, proxies, and downloaders, this can lead to disclosure of sensitive local files. Existence of files can also be inferred through differing error responses even when content is not directly observable.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in GStreamer's gst-plugins-good, specifically in the H.264 RTP depayloader element. When processing MTAP16 or MTAP24 multi-time aggregation RTP packets, a signed/unsigned integer conversion error causes the remaining-length counter to underflow to a large positive value when the packet is truncated. This allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to trigger an out-of-bounds heap read of up to approximately 64 KiB of process memory by sending a single malformed RTP packet. Successful exploitation can crash the receiving GStreamer pipeline (denial of service), and in relay or transcoding deployments where output is accessible to the attacker, may expose adjacent heap contents.

descriptions.value: FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in tgv_decode_inter() in libavcodec/eatgv.c that ignores init_get_bits() failure on oversized packets. Attackers can supply a crafted EA file with a kVGT frame followed by an fVGT inter frame with a 2^28-byte compressed block section, crashing the process for denial of service.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in the Cirrus Logic AccuPak (CLJR) decoder in libavcodec/cljrdec.c because decode_frame() ignores init_get_bits() failure. Attackers can supply a crafted AVI file with a 2^28-byte CLJR frame that overflows the bit count, causing reads from a NULL buffer and crashing the process.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in vble_decode_frame() in libavcodec/vble.c because it ignores init_get_bits() failure on oversized packets. Attackers can supply a crafted AVI file with a 268435452-byte VBLE frame, causing reads from a NULL bit reader buffer that crash the process.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in the Bink video decoder because decode_frame() in libavcodec/bink.c ignores init_get_bits() failure. Attackers can supply a crafted Bink file with a frame of about 2^28 bytes, overflowing the bit count and crashing the process for denial of service.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in libxevd_receive_frame() in libavcodec/libxevd.c that fails to validate NAL unit length prefixes against remaining packet data. Attackers can supply crafted EVC media with oversized 4-byte NAL length prefixes, causing libxevd to read past the packet buffer, crashing the application or exposing adjacent heap memory.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a memory leak vulnerability in libxevd_receive_frame() in libavcodec/libxevd.c that fails to free pkt_au when an access unit produces no picture. Attackers can supply a crafted EVC stream with many access units containing only parameter sets or non-frame NAL units to exhaust memory in the decoding application.

FFmpeg before 8.1.3 and 9.x before 9.0.2 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in ff_hap_set_chunk_count() in libavcodec/hap.c, where a shadowed return variable masks reallocation failures. Attackers can supply a crafted Hap video frame with an oversized chunk count so the decoder writes through a NULL chunk table, crashing the application.

A flaw was found in Red Hat Quay. An unauthenticated client can obtain an anonymous registry token with an audience it controls, present that token to the service key rotation endpoint, and install its own approved signing key with no expiry. Registry tokens signed with that key are accepted for any repository, allowing read and write access to private images and replacement of repository tags.

affectedData.product: mirror registry for Red Hat OpenShift 2.0

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in Quay where the robot account listing function constructs a SQL LIKE pattern from user-controlled namespace names without escaping wildcard metacharacters. An attacker who creates a namespace containing an underscore character can match and retrieve robot accounts and their decrypted authentication tokens from other tenants' namespaces, leading to cross-tenant credential theft and unauthorized image operations.
